That margin line is the one HPE was sold about 16% on today despite beating and raising.

next_guide.street_next_quarter: Not found directly. Derived: street FY27 revenue $194.3B (247wallst 2026-11-19) minus H1 actual $90.8B and Q3 consensus $50.63B implies about $52.9B for Q4.
next_guide.company_current_guide: FY27 revenue $192.0B +/- $2B, non-GAAP EPS $25.50, AI server revenue $74B (SEC exhibit, 2026-09-01). Implied Q4 is about $52.2B revenue and about $22.5B AI server revenue (192 - 43.8 - 47.0 - 49.0; 74 - 16.1 - 16.4 - 19).
next_guide.basis: Dell has raised the FY guide three quarters running and beat the Q2 guide midpoint by about $2.5B. The $95B backlog is supply-gated, not demand-gated (Schmoock 2026-10-21; HPE says components are constrained into calendar 2028). Counterparties NVDA and HPE printed strong Aug-Oct quarters, so a revenue raise to at least the ~$194B street is likely. The margin and EPS guide is the open question given Q4 DRAM contract inflation and HPE's FY27 margin step-down.

findings.finding: Nvidia's Q3 FY27 (quarter ended 2026-10-25, overlapping Dell's Aug-Oct quarter) had Data Center revenue of $107.6B (+110% y/y). Revenue from AI cloud, industrial and enterprise customers, the segment Dell sells into, was $47.5B, +195% y/y, against +71% for hyperscalers. Q4 is guided to $130B. This supports Dell shipping at or above its ~$19B AI server guide and keeping orders strong.
findings.link: Nvidia supplies the GPUs in Dell's AI-optimized servers ($16.4B of Dell's $47.0B Q2 revenue). Nvidia's 'AI cloud, industrial and enterprise' bucket is the neocloud/sovereign/enterprise channel Dell serves; Bernstein puts emerging AI clouds at about 27% of Dell FY27 revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dell's last three prints, each with an AI revenue beat and orders surprise, moved +15.8%, +32.8% and +21.9% (baseline). The two before them, with smaller AI beats, moved -8.9% and -2.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and the AI-server group traded on it, but Dell fell 7% on Nov 16 and then another ~10% on Nov 24, so the price has not followed the counterparty. If it had, Dell would not sit about 11-12x forward EPS and 49% under its high while its GPU supplier guides +12% q/q.
findings.independence: HPE's same-quarter server revenue +95% (SEC 8-K ex-99.1, 2026-11-23) and SMCI's Q1 FY27 beat (SEC 8-K) are separate documents pointing the same way.

findings.finding: HPE's fiscal Q4 (Aug-Oct 2026, the same three months as Dell's Q3): server revenue $8.79B (+94.7% y/y, ASP-driven with supply-constrained units). Cloud & AI operating margin 18.4%, above HPE's guide and up from 9.3%. AI systems orders $4.5B (+130%). Revenue $14.5B against $14.35B consensus and EPS $1.43 against $1.27. A direct same-quarter read that server pricing and margins held for Dell's ISG.
findings.link: Direct competitor in the same products (x86 and AI servers, storage), same fiscal quarter Aug-Oct, same component constraints; HPE servers are $8.8B against Dell ISG's $31.8B in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dell's ISG margin surprise in Q2 (15.0% against 10.5% in Q1) came with +15.8%. Barclays' Oct 15 cut on hardware margins moved Dell -8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The market priced HPE's guide, not its quarter: Dell fell about 10% the day after a same-quarter peer printed server margins above guide. If the quarter read-through were priced, Dell would have risen or held on Nov 24.
findings.independence: Same document as the HPE-guide finding below, read for a different line (the reported quarter against the forward margin guide). Nvidia's release is independent.

findings.finding: HPE's FY27 guide moderates Cloud & AI margin to about 14% from 15.2%. Management said component costs are 'rising faster than pricing', expects gross margin to moderate in H2 as AI mix rises, and sees memory/NAND constrained into at least H2 calendar 2028. HPE closed +17.4% on Nov 23, then fell 6.7% after hours and about 16% on Nov 24 despite beating and raising revenue. That is a live analog for a Dell beat-and-raise being sold on the margin outlook.
findings.link: Same products, same fiscal quarter, same memory suppliers; Dell guides Q4 (Nov-Jan) and HPE guided Q1 (Nov-Jan), the same calendar months.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dell's Aug 2025 print (-8.9%) and Nov 2024 print (-12.2%, Unusual Whales table) were margin-led selloffs. Its last three guide raises were bought.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced already: Dell fell about 10% on Nov 24 alongside HPE. What is not priced is whether Dell repeats the step-down. If the market were sure Dell would guide margins down like HPE, the skew would be steeper than +3.56 and the straddle would carry a larger downside premium.
findings.independence: TrendForce's Q4 2026 DRAM contract outlook (separate source) points the same way on cost. Morgan Stanley's memory-cost downgrade is a 2025 story and is excluded.

findings.finding: TrendForce projects conventional DRAM contract prices +10-15% q/q in 4Q26 and server DIMM contract prices +10%+ q/q, and its Oct 30 update says server DRAM prices kept climbing in October. That inflates Dell's Q4 (Nov-Jan) bill of materials in both ISG and CSG; CSG PC margins are already guided to about 6%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dell fell -8.9% in Aug 2025, when margins compressed on AI mix and component costs. The Q2 FY27 margin expansion came with pricing discipline and +15.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Industry series, public for weeks. Its transmission into Dell's Q4 margin guide depends on Dell's pass-through, which only the call reveals. If it were fully priced, HPE's similar commentary would not have taken that stock down 16%.
findings.independence: This is a proxy and is sized small. HPE's management commentary (separate source) confirms commodity costs rising faster than pricing.

findings.finding: Super Micro's Q1 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026): net sales $19.9B, EPS $1.81 against a $1.01-1.10 guide, FY27 revenue guide raised to $72-82B from $65-72B, gross margin 12.7%. AI-server demand and pricing held through the first two months of Dell's quarter.
findings.link: Same product (Nvidia-based AI rack servers), same neocloud/enterprise customer channel; SMCI's quarter overlaps August-September of Dell's Aug-Oct quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not this name's line directly. Dell fell with SMCI's weak margin print in Nov 2025 (per a gurufocus headline).
findings.why_not_priced: It is three weeks old and Dell has fallen since, so it is largely absorbed. It still says demand did not crack mid-quarter, which the -41% drawdown implicitly questions.
findings.independence: Nvidia's release and HPE's 8-K are separate documents.

findings.link: CoreWeave is a neocloud and a buyer of AI servers. Bernstein puts emerging AI cloud customers at about 27% of Dell FY27 revenue; the source does not name CoreWeave as a Dell customer.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dell rose +12% on 2026-11-11 on this read-through, which shows the stock trades on neocloud demand signals.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced on the day (+12%) and since given back. It matters again only through Dell's orders figure tonight.
findings.independence: Nvidia's +195% in AI cloud/enterprise customers is a separate source pointing the same way.

findings.finding: Consensus already sits above the company guide: revenue $50.63B against the $49.0B guide (+3.3%), EPS $6.63 against $6.50, whisper $7.25. Other sources put EPS at $6.62 and $6.76. Dell beat its Q2 revenue guide midpoint by about 5.6%; a repeat would be about $51.7B, roughly 2% above consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY27 beat its guide by about $2.5B, with an FY raise, and the stock moved +15.8%. Unusual Whales: realised move exceeded implied in 7 of 12 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar sits above the guide by design. The open question is whether Dell clears the whisper ($7.25), and the sources disagree on consensus, so this finding is capped small.
findings.independence: Unusual Whales gives $6.76 EPS consensus (https://unusualwhales.com/news/dell-technologies-earnings-preview-implied-move-2026-11-24), which conflicts with $6.63, so the bar is disputed.

findings.finding: Into the print the stock is -40.7% over 20 days and about 49% off its Sept 17 high. It fell 43% from Oct 9 to Nov 10, against about 33% for SMCI and HPE. Trefis attributes each large down day to non-Dell causes: post-midterm data-center fears on Nov 5 (-14.9%), Nvidia CEO turmoil on Nov 13 (-7.2%) and the chip selloff on Nov 16 (-7.0%). The stock trades at about 11-12x forward EPS against a 5-year average of about 12x. This is a low-expectation setup into a company whose own numbers have not been cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 (+21.9%) came after a 29% drawdown into the print (barchart headline 'Dell stock drops 29% ... ahead of Feb 26'). In Sep 2026 the stock fell 4% the day before and rose +15.8% after.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown itself is the price. The claim is that it holds macro and sector de-rating that a company print can partly reverse; if the market had priced Dell's own fundamentals down, consensus FY EPS would have fallen, and it has risen to $25.97-26.01, above the $25.50 guide.
findings.independence: Stockanalysis (2026-11-11) gives the peer-relative drawdown; tikr/Bernstein (2026-11-18) say 'none of it came from Dell's own results'. Lesson 5 caution: this argues from the absence of a company cause, and today's HPE-driven -10% is a cause.

findings.finding: Dell's reaction function: the last three prints, each a beat with a guide raise, moved +15.8%, +32.8% and +21.9%. Across 12 prints the realised move exceeded the implied move 7 times, averaging 13.6% against 7.8% implied. Beats on this name have been bought, not sold, in the AI era.
findings.why_not_priced: Options price ±8.4-11.4% with downside skew, so the market is not paying for an upside follow-through at the scale this history shows.
findings.independence: Baseline history (8-K acceptance times) independently gives the same moves.

findings.finding: Next guide: the current FY27 guide of $192B implies Q4 about $52.2B, against a street-implied Q4 of about $52.9B (FY street $194.3B). AI server guide $74B implies about $22.5B in Q4. With a $95B backlog that is supply-gated, a fourth consecutive FY revenue raise to at least the street is the likely outcome. The EPS/margin piece is open: street FY EPS is $25.97-26.01 against the $25.50 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY raises: Q1 FY27 (FY to $165-169B, AI to $60B) gave +32.8%; Q2 FY27 (to $192B, AI to $74B) gave +15.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The street at $194.3B already embeds a small raise. A raise that only meets it, with margin caution like HPE's, would be sold. The positive value here is the size of a backlog-backed raise (the Q2 raise was $25B), which the -41% drawdown says the market doubts.
findings.independence: HPE raised its FY27 revenue growth range to 27-35% (SEC 8-K 2026-11-23), an independent peer raise on the same demand. Nvidia guides Q4 +12% q/q.

findings.finding: Mid-quarter statement, 2026-10-21: Dell SVP of global revenue operations David Schmoock said AI demand still outpaces supply, the market has entered 'cost inflation', and projects without early planning have been delayed 60-120 days. Revenue conversion is supply-gated rather than demand-gated, and pricing power is intact.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No price reaction recorded to this interview.
findings.why_not_priced: A low-profile trade interview, not a reaffirmation. It cuts both ways (strong demand, but 60-120 day slips could cap Q3 conversion), so it is sized at zero.
findings.independence: HPE's commentary on 28-40+ week component lead times (investing.com transcript) says the same about supply gating.

findings.finding: Dell raised $5B of notes in September to fund the hardware ramp. Net debt is $23.6B, financing receivables rose to $20.4B at Jul 31 from $14.3B six months earlier, and Q2 operating cash flow was $2.2B (-13% y/y). Previews (tikr) frame free cash flow as a key test tonight.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY27 printed OCF -13% y/y and the stock still rose 15.8%, so FCF has not decided a recent reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Asked what the money buys: the answer is a corroborated ramp ($95B backlog, $60.9B Q2 orders), so the financing itself is a zero. The small negative is FCF optics in a market that just punished a peer on quality, and the receivables growth Bernstein's critics cite (tikr 2026-11-18).
findings.independence: Receivables figure from the tikr Bernstein piece (separate article, same publisher).

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly long, against a moderate downside skew (+3.56) and with the 20-day drawdown (a low bar). The strongest single item, HPE being sold about 16% on a beat-and-raise today, agrees with the skew and keeps p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the three same-quarter counterparty/peer findings (NVDA, HPE quarter, SMCI) were cut from +1.0/+1.0/+0.5 to +0.7/+0.7/+0.3, because HPE's own beat was sold today.
Lesson 5 (absence of a company cause is not evidence): the drawdown/low-bar expectations finding was cut from +2.0 to +1.0. Today's -10% has a sourced cause (HPE's margin guide).
Lesson 6 (bar disputed): consensus EPS sources disagree ($6.62/$6.63/$6.76) and revenue consensus has one source; the consensus finding is kept at +0.3, capped small.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the $5B notes fund a corroborated ramp ($95B backlog), so the financing finding moved from -0.5 to -0.3, with only FCF optics left.
Insider finding resized from -0.3 to -0.1 after reading the Form 144 itself (2,022 shares, $766k).
Lesson 7: skew moderate and short interest light; the HPE-guide negative was kept at -2.0 because there is no squeeze mechanism to shrink it.
p_up moved from 56 to 54 (caveats toward 50); abs_move_pct unchanged at 13.
